## Natural history notes

A medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish-brown forewings with darker patches, pale lines, and a sturdy body typical of cutworm moths. In Florida, the Green Cutworm Moth is found in fields, gardens, lawns, roadsides, pastures, wetlands, forest edges, and other open or disturbed habitats with low herbaceous vegetation. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and broadleaf plants near the ground, sometimes cutting or damaging young plants and serving as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
